passages.text: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
passages.sermon:
You judge other people.
You have no excuse.
When you judge someone else, you also judge yourself.
You do the same things that you judge in others.
You condemn yourself by your own judgment.
passages.original: Διὸ ἀναπολόγητος εἶ ὦ ἄνθρωπε πᾶς ὁ κρίνων ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίνεις τὸν ἕτερον σεαυτὸν κατακρίνεις τὰ γὰρ αὐτὰ πράσσεις ὁ κρίνων

passages.text: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
passages.sermon: God judges people who do such things.\r\nGod’s judgment is always true.\r\nWe know this.
passages.original: οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τὸ κρίμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας

passages.text: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to people who judge others.
Paul says these people also do the same wrong things.
Paul asks a question.
He says, “You judge others for their sins.”
“You do the same sins yourself.”
“Do you think you will escape God’s judgment?”
passages.original: λογίζῃ δὲ τοῦτο ὦ ἄνθρωπε ὁ κρίνων τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας καὶ ποιῶν αὐτά ὅτι σὺ ἐκφεύξῃ τὸ κρίμα τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
passages.sermon:
God is kind.
God is tolerant.
God is patient.
God shows great kindness, tolerance, and patience to people.
You may ignore or look down on these riches of God’s kindness, tolerance, and patience.
You may not realize something important.
God’s kindness leads you to repentance.
passages.original: ἢ τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀνοχῆς καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας καταφρονεῖς ἀγνοῶν ὅτι τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιάν σε ἄγει

passages.text: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
passages.sermon:
You have a hard heart.
You do not repent.
Because of this, you store up wrath for yourself.
A day of wrath is coming.
On that day, God will reveal His righteous judgment.
passages.original: Κατὰ δὲ τὴν σκληρότητά σου καὶ ἀμετανόητον καρδίαν θησαυρίζεις σεαυτῷ ὀργὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὀργῆς καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως δικαιοκρισίας τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”
passages.sermon:
God is the judge.
God will repay each person.
God will judge based on what each person has done.
God will give to each one according to his deeds.
passages.original: ὃς Ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
passages.sermon:
God judges every person.
Some people do good works.
They keep doing good with patience.
They seek glory.
They seek honor.
They seek immortality.
God gives these people eternal life.
passages.original: τοῖς μὲν καθ’ ὑπομονὴν ἔργου ἀγαθοῦ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν ζητοῦσιν ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.
passages.sermon:
God judges every person.
God looks at each person's actions.
Some people are self-seeking.
These people reject the truth.
They choose to follow wickedness.
God will give wrath and anger to these people.
passages.original: τοῖς δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας καὶ ἀπειθοῦσι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πειθομένοις δὲ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ ὀργὴ καὶ θυμός

passages.text: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek; but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.
passages.sermon:
God judges every person fairly.
God does not show favoritism.
Every person who does evil will face trouble and distress.
This includes every human being.
God will judge the Jew first.
God will also judge the Greek.
Every person who does good will receive glory, honor, and peace.
This includes everyone who does good.
God will reward the Jew first.
God will also reward the Greek.
passages.original: θλῖψις καὶ στενοχωρία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου τοῦ κατεργαζομένου τὸ κακόν Ἰουδαίου τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνος δόξα δὲ καὶ τιμὴ καὶ εἰρήνη παντὶ τῷ ἐργαζομένῳ τὸ ἀγαθόν Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι

passages.text: For God does not show favoritism.
passages.sermon:
God does not show favoritism.
God treats everyone equally.
God judges all people fairly.
God does not prefer one person over another.
passages.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν προσωπολημψία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
passages.sermon:
God judges every person fairly.
Some people sin without knowing the law.
These people will perish without the law.
Other people sin while knowing the law.
These people will be judged by the law.
passages.original: Ὅσοι γὰρ ἀνόμως ἥμαρτον ἀνόμως καὶ ἀπολοῦνται καὶ ὅσοι ἐν νόμῳ ἥμαρτον διὰ νόμου κριθήσονται

passages.text: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.
passages.sermon:
God does not show favoritism.
God judges everyone fairly.
Hearing the law does not make a person righteous before God.
Doing what the law says makes a person righteous before God.
God declares the doers of the law righteous.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ οἱ ἀκροαταὶ νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἀλλ’ οἱ ποιηταὶ νόμου δικαιωθήσονται

passages.text: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
passages.sermon:
Gentiles are people who are not Jews.
Gentiles do not have the law of Moses.
Sometimes Gentiles do what the law requires.
They do these things by nature.
Gentiles do not have the law.
But they act as if they have a law for themselves.
They become a law to themselves.
passages.original: Ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος

passages.text: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.
passages.sermon:
Gentiles do not have the law.
They do what the law requires by nature.
They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts.
Their consciences also bear witness.
Their thoughts sometimes accuse them.
Their thoughts sometimes defend them.
God will judge the secrets of people.
God will do this through Christ Jesus.
My gospel proclaims this truth.
passages.original: οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ὅτε κρίνει ὁ Θεὸς τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου διὰ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God; if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law; if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness, an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth— you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Jews who know the law.
You call yourself a Jew.
You rely on the law.
You boast in God.
You know God’s will.
You approve what is superior.
You learn these things from the law.
You believe you are a guide for the blind.
You believe you are a light for those in darkness.
You believe you are an instructor of the foolish.
You believe you are a teacher of infants.
You have in the law the form of knowledge and truth.
You teach others.
Do you teach yourself?
You preach that people should not steal.
Do you steal?
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ἐπονομάζῃ καὶ ἐπαναπαύῃ νόμῳ καὶ καυχᾶσαι ἐν Θεῷ καὶ γινώσκεις τὸ θέλημα καὶ δοκιμάζεις τὰ διαφέροντα κατηχούμενος ἐκ τοῦ νόμου πέποιθάς τε σεαυτὸν ὁδηγὸν εἶναι τυφλῶν φῶς τῶν ἐν σκότει παιδευτὴν ἀφρόνων διδάσκαλον νηπίων ἔχοντα τὴν μόρφωσιν τῆς γνώσεως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὁ οὖν διδάσκων ἕτερον σεαυτὸν οὐ διδάσκεις ὁ κηρύσσων μὴ κλέπτειν κλέπτεις

passages.text: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
passages.sermon:
Paul addresses Jews who know the law and teach others.
You say, “Do not commit adultery.”
But do you commit adultery?
You say you hate idols.
But do you rob temples?
passages.original: ὁ λέγων μὴ μοιχεύειν μοιχεύεις ὁ βδελυσσόμενος τὰ εἴδωλα ἱεροσυλεῖς

passages.text: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
passages.sermon:
You are a Jew.
You boast in the law.
You break the law.
You dishonor God by breaking the law.
passages.original: ὃς ἐν νόμῳ καυχᾶσαι διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου τὸν Θεὸν ἀτιμάζεις

passages.text: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
passages.sermon:
God’s name is holy.
God’s name is important among all people.
Some people claim to follow God’s law.
These people break God’s law.
Because of their actions, others speak evil of God’s name.
The Gentiles see this.
The Gentiles blaspheme God’s name because of these people.
Scripture says this happens.
passages.original: τὸ γὰρ Ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ δι’ ὑμᾶς βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καθὼς γέγραπται

passages.text: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
passages.sermon:
Circumcision is a physical sign for Jewish people.
Circumcision helps you only if you obey the law.
If you break the law, circumcision does not help you.
If you break the law, your circumcision is counted as if you were not circumcised.
passages.original: Περιτομὴ μὲν γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἐὰν νόμον πράσσῃς ἐὰν δὲ παραβάτης νόμου ᾖς ἡ περιτομή σου ἀκροβυστία γέγονεν

passages.text: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
passages.sermon:
A man may not be circumcised.
He may still obey the law’s requirements.
If he obeys the law, God sees his obedience.
God will count his uncircumcision as if he were circumcised.
passages.original: ἐὰν οὖν ἡ ἀκροβυστία τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ νόμου φυλάσσῃ οὐχ ἡ ἀκροβυστία αὐτοῦ εἰς περιτομὴν λογισθήσεται

passages.text: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
passages.sermon:
A person may be physically uncircumcised.
This person may keep the law.
This person obeys what God commands.
You have the written law.
You have circumcision.
You break the law.
The uncircumcised person who keeps the law will judge you.
You have the law and circumcision, but you do not obey.
Obedience matters more than outward signs.
passages.original: καὶ κρινεῖ ἡ ἐκ φύσεως ἀκροβυστία τὸν νόμον τελοῦσα σὲ τὸν διὰ γράμματος καὶ περιτομῆς παραβάτην νόμου

passages.text: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
passages.sermon:
A true Jew is not just someone who appears to be a Jew on the outside.
Circumcision is not only something done outwardly to the body.
Being a Jew is not about outward appearance.
Circumcision is not just a physical act.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν οὐδὲ ἡ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ ἐν σαρκὶ περιτομή

passages.text: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.
passages.sermon:
A true Jew is a person who is a Jew inwardly.
This person’s identity is not just outward or physical.
Circumcision for this person is a matter of the heart.
The Holy Spirit does this work in the heart.
The written law does not do this work.
God gives praise to this person.
People do not give this praise.
God alone gives approval to the one who is a Jew inwardly and has a changed heart by the Spirit.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ Ἰουδαῖος καὶ περιτομὴ καρδίας ἐν πνεύματι οὐ γράμματι οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλ’ ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ
